name: Select a patient-RNA splicing-variant validation workflow
description: Which DNA/RNA evidence workflow identifies splice-altering variants for inherited-disorder follow-up when patient RNA and tissue-specific context are available?

attributes.question: Which DNA/RNA evidence workflow identifies splice-altering variants for inherited-disorder follow-up when patient RNA and tissue-specific context are available?
intended_users: Clinical researchers scoping the available diagnostic-genomics evidence
Computational researchers comparing exact evaluated configurations
attributes.decision: Inspect the FRASER known pathogenic-event recovery curve and the sequence-classification proxy evidence before selecting a workflow and designing patient-RNA follow-up for the intended cohort size.
inputs: Patient skin-fibroblast (or matched tissue) RNA-seq aligned reads
The number of samples available for a FRASER-style aberrant-splicing cohort
attributes.output: A sourced recovery curve (fraction of known pathogenic splicing events recovered as cohort size grows) and a separate sequence-classification proxy; no diagnostic-yield claim for unknown cases.
attributes.setting: FRASER, applied to a retrospective Kremer rare-mitochondrial-disorder skin-fibroblast RNA cohort (119 samples/105 individuals, 13 known pathogenic splicing events), recovers a mean 85% (11 of 13) of known events at a reduced 30-sample subsample. Separate, proxy sequence-classification results for DNA foundation models (Alavi et al. 2026: Evo 2 40B, Genos 10B and NTv3 650M classifying variants with established splicing defects against benign variants) are also linked, scoped as a different endpoint. Feng et al. 2025 Table 1 splice acceptor and donor classification is linked to 'Prioritise variants for splicing experiments', not here.
exclusions: Diagnostic yield in patients without a known pathogenic event (this is recovery of already-known events, not discovery)
Full-cohort outlier-gene workload counts (12/7/10 genes/sample), a different population from the 30-sample recovery evaluation and not ingested here
Blinded pathogenicity adjudication or VUS reclassification
attributes.clinical_scope: Clinical applicability is not established beyond known-event recovery. This does not demonstrate prospective diagnostic yield, blinded adjudication, or general tissue transfer.
evidence_gaps: No numeric confidence interval is reported for the 85% recovery figure in the inspected main text.
Subsampling repeat count and exact score-aggregation method are unextracted.

Feng et al. 2025 Table 1 splice-site classification is not linked to this use case: it measures AUC on benchmark splice-site sequences (DNABERT-2/NT datasets), not patient RNA, and is linked to 'Prioritise variants for splicing experiments'. The DNA foundation-model results linked here (Alavi et al. 2026: Evo 2 40B, Genos 10B and NTv3 650M) are threshold classifications of variants with established splicing defects, also proxies; none recovers events from patient RNA-seq.

AbSplice (Wagner et al. 2023, Nat Genet) reports its tissue-aware comparison with SpliceAI, MMSplice, SQUIRLS and CADD-Splice only in figures and prose in the copies screened, so no tissue-aware DNA predictor comparison is stored.
The FRASER 2.0 article (Scheller et al. 2023, AJHG) could not be retrieved as full text, and its comparison with FRASER, LeafCutterMD and SPOT on patient cohorts was not extracted.
No table comparing MMSplice, CADD-Splice or AbSplice against RNA-validated variants was found in this pass; Drost et al. cover SpliceAI, Pangolin, SPiP and SQUIRLS only.
Drost et al. variant-type strata (Data S1 Tables S5 and S6) are not extracted.
False positives are tabulated only as true-negative samples with any outlier (Silverstein et al. 2026, Table S9); outlier counts per sample remain figure-only.
Minigene or MFASS-style proxies beyond the existing MFASS mapping were not added in this pass.
MAJIQ-CLIN (Genet Med 2026) compares splicing outlier tools but could not be retrieved as full text.
Silverstein et al. 2026 expression-outlier true-negative counts conflict between Tables S7 and S9, so the OUTRIDER rows are not linked.
No machine-learning method has been compared with FRASER or OUTRIDER on the same patient RNA data in the linked evidence.
